# Rules and process fixes

## bm_store.py verify() problems at generation time

None. If a process fix belongs here anyway, it is one this session found some other way; write it in below.

## Notes (human, preserved verbatim on regeneration)

<!-- bm-human:begin -->
FOUR PROCESS FIXES, each earned by something going wrong.

1. RUN THE GATE ON A COMMITTED, CLEAN TREE, AND ALWAYS WITH --artifacts. Dirty-tree runs make the gate blame the suites for your own uncommitted files, and without artifacts a failure leaves only a one-line verdict, costing a twenty minute re-run to recover the reason.

2. ONE INSTALL-CLASS SUITE AT A TIME ON THIS MACHINE, whoever runs it and FROM WHEREVER. A worktree isolates FILES; it does not isolate SIDE EFFECTS. tools/test_install.py performs real checkout installs, so two copies compete for the same temp and git state even from different working copies. This cost a forty minute run. The existing fold protocol covered WRITES and had no clause for READS.

3. PO-6 IS A SEARCH, NOT AN ACTION. A new shipping file or a new command line verb joins MORE registries than the one you are thinking of. A verb added here had to join three: the effect-class registry, the runtime adapters, and the founder-facing refusal table. Checking one and declaring the rule satisfied is the failure; docs/mistakes/M21 carries the reconnaissance command.

4. A FOURTH RECOVERY IS MISSING FROM EVERY WRITE-BOUNDARY CONTROL: touch nothing, name the owner, report as accurate but unactionable. Three controls were RIGHT about the state and offered no legal way out, because all three are written for a single writer discovering their own mess and have no vocabulary for a shared tree with two live writers.
